tldr.title: In short
tldr.body: If your customers should order ahead on their phone and choose a collection time, you need an ordering system, not just a till. Look for four things: collection times that follow your kitchen capacity; a weekly schedule for changing locations; low or no fees per order; and no long contract. Card readers and tills cover payment at the truck and complement an ordering system.

fit.title: Which system suits whom?
fit.oursBody: you trade at changing locations, want pre-orders with a collection time, don't want your kitchen overloaded, and don't want a contract.
fit.oursNotBody: your customers should pay with PayPal or Klarna, or you want a certified till with a TSE from one supplier.
fit.appClause: Or if you need the kitchen app on iPad or Android in {country}: it isn't in the stores there yet.
fit.tillsBody: Tills take payment at the truck and cover the TSE requirement — for example SumUp, Zettle (PayPal), orderbird and ready2order, by their own websites. Of those four, only SumUp offers pre-ordering with a chosen collection time, on its Kassensystem Plus plan. An ordering system works alongside a till; it does not replace it.
fit.marketplacesBody: Delivery platforms bring new customers but take commission on every order. Uber Eats states 14% for collection and 30% for delivery by Uber couriers in Germany. Wolt says on its own website that it charges commission but gives no rates. We could not check Lieferando’s rates. That commission applies to regulars who pre-order with you, too.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.whatQ: What is a food truck ordering system?
faq.whatA: An ordering system takes orders online before customers reach the truck: they choose dishes and a collection time, pay online or on collection, and the order appears in your kitchen. A till or card machine takes payment at the truck. The two complement each other.
faq.costA: {plans}. Online card payments also carry Stripe’s fees: {cardFee} per card payment.
faq.termA: No. There is no minimum term and no notice period. You can cancel any time; the fee is billed monthly in advance, and you keep access until the end of the month you have paid for.
faq.locationsQ: Does it work with changing locations?
faq.locationsA: Yes. You set up your weekly schedule with places and times, and customers order for the place and the day you are there.
faq.capacityQ: How does the system stop my kitchen being overloaded?
faq.capacityA: Customers only see collection times your kitchen can actually make. The system works from each dish's preparation time and how many you prepare at once.
faq.tseQ: Do I still need a till with a TSE?
faq.tseA: HatchGrab is not a till and has no TSE. How you record online orders in your till is a question for your tax adviser.
faq.paymentsQ: Which payment methods does HatchGrab support?
faq.paymentsA: Customers pay online by card, Apple Pay or Google Pay, or pay at the truck. PayPal and Klarna are not supported at the moment.
